A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 6DGS work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering-quality, Gaussian-count, speed, and ablation results on its custom rendered dataset and Synthetic NeRF.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds real-world evaluations, a subsurface-scattering scene, and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The conditional Gaussian slicing, spherical-harmonic colors, learnable opacity modulation, and adaptive Gaussian control remain unchanged. The revised SVD notation and added Python listing describe the existing procedure rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 add Deep Blending, Tanks & Temples, Shiny, and a dragon scene combining subsurface and surface scattering. This substantially extends evaluation to captured indoor, outdoor, and reflective scenes and another light-transport scenario. The original six-scene 6DGS-PBRT dataset is retained under the name 6DGS-PBR.

E2.justification: The matched original experiments retain 3DGS and N-DG. New Deep Blending, Tanks & Temples, and dragon comparisons use these existing baselines; Shiny compares against 3DGS alone. NeX is cited for data and settings, not evaluated as a new comparator. The FlashGS variant already appeared in v1.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated learnable-opacity training interval from iterations 150,000–280,000 to 15,000–28,000, a substantial tenfold revision to the reported schedule. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. New evaluations also specify Shiny image resizing and introduce training time as a comparison metric; original splits and image-quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SH, opacity, lambda, and pruning-threshold ablations are retained unchanged, including v1 Table 5 becoming v3 Table 8. v3 adds a focused mixed-scattering case study with geometry visualizations in A.2 and a training-cost analysis in A.5.

E5.justification: Both versions describe FPS averaging over 20 test images with 500 repeated measurements per image. Neither reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests, and the additions introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original numerical tables are retained, but v3 adds substantial results in Tables 5–7 and 9. New comparisons include Deep Blending PSNR of 28.59 for 6DGS versus 29.48 for 3DGS, Shiny averages of 23.01 versus 22.44, and dragon PSNR of 35.00 versus 26.57 for 3DGS and 33.19 for N-DG. Table 9 adds average training times of 36, 30, and 96 minutes, respectively.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, conditioning equations, and theoretical discussion are retained. Replacing the general SVD notation with the equivalent symmetric covariance decomposition changes notation rather than mathematical substance; no new assumptions, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: improved directional color and opacity modeling, adaptive control, 3DGS compatibility, and conditional-Gaussian analysis. The headline maximum PSNR improvement of 15.73 dB and Gaussian reduction of 66.5% are unchanged.

C2.justification: A.1, A.2, and A.5 add interpretations concerning real-world generalization, mixed light transport, compactness-versus-quality tradeoffs, and training overhead. These extend the existing interpretation without changing the proposed mechanism. The new broad language about quality improvements across datasets is stronger than the mixed outcomes in Tables 5–6 support.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page pointer, a Python slicing implementation, training-time information, and settings for added evaluations, while retaining the original hardware and optimizer details. Listing 1 has an undefined x and inconsistent refinement-variable names, limiting its usability. The project-page pointer alone does not establish code or dataset availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references associated with Deep Blending, Tanks & Temples, and NeX/Shiny, and includes the already-cited Gao et al. work in the related-work discussion. Its substantive positioning relative to 3DGS, N-DG, and Gaussian ray tracing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. Edits include PBRT-to-PBR terminology, ray/path-tracing wording, covariance notation, and publication/author annotations. The appendix gains descriptive subsections A.1–A.6 and separates previously adjacent explanations and ablation material.

P2.justification: v3 adds four result tables, three qualitative-comparison figures, and a formatted code listing, substantially expanding the visual evidence. Existing figures are retained: v1 Figures 4–5 become v3 Figures 5–6, and v1 Table 5 becomes v3 Table 8, with relocation and resizing rather than replacement.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's lack of validation on captured real-world scenes and its missing training-cost comparison. Tables 5–7 and 9 make practical applicability and quality-versus-efficiency tradeoffs much more assessable, including cases where fewer Gaussians accompany lower image quality. Overgeneralized interpretation of these mixed results and errors in the new code listing limit the gains, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
